implementation_notes: Default platform realization: one shared center is the hub, Notification.Name values are the channels, and the token returned by addObserver(forName:object:queue:using:) is removed with removeObserver(_:). The queue parameter decides where handlers run, so UI delivery needs queue: .main; prefer the message-based APIs (MainActorMessage/AsyncMessage) when actor isolation and typed payloads are required.
pitfalls: Forgetting removeObserver(token) leaks the closure and everything it captures for the lifetime of the process.
Selector-based observers (addObserver(_:selector:name:object:)) require explicit removal and crash-prone unregistering order in deinit compared with the block API.

variants.name: Combine PassthroughSubject / AnyPublisher
variants.implementation_notes: Reactive realization: a subject is the hub, send() publishes, and every subscriber gets a Cancellable that is also the unsubscribe handle (retaining it is what keeps the subscription alive). Operators add the filtering, mapping and merging a NotificationCenter observer would have to hand-code, and NotificationCenter.publisher(for:) turns the system hub into the same stream shape - at the price of never completing, so the Cancellable must be managed explicitly.
pitfalls: A Cancellable that is not retained is cancelled immediately, so the subscription appears to do nothing.

PassthroughSubject drops values sent before any subscriber arrives and after completion - it is state-free by design; use CurrentValueSubject or a replaying publisher when late subscribers need history.
Combine is delivery-controlled but not thread-safe across arbitrary queues; publish on one scheduler (receive(on:)) to avoid re-entrancy surprises.
